root.name: King's Indian Defense: Steiner Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. f3 O-O 6. Bg5

overview: A sharper version of the Sämisch where White adds 6.Bg5 to the f3 and e4 centre, aiming for Qd2, O-O-O and a kingside pawn storm. Black replies with ...c5, and after 7.d5 usually ...e6 or ...a6 reaches Benoni-style structures, with queenside play and ...b5 breaks against White's space and attack. The game often features opposite-wing action, though it is less forcing than the main Sämisch lines.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the Bg5 and Qd2 for a quick O-O-O
Push d5 to gain space and fix the centre
Advance g4/h4 for a pawn storm if Black castles short

black_ideas.idea: After 7.d5 play ...e6 or ...a6 and ...b5 to create queenside play
Use ...h6 or ...Nc6/...e5 to put the Bg5 question to White

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-type centre with White pawns on c4, d5, e4 and f3 against Black c5, d6
King's Indian locked centre with opposite-side attacks

character.notes: Space and a kingside pawn storm for White against Black counterplay on the queenside; typical King's Indian sharp play.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound for both; the Bg5 sideline is a respected attacking weapon with no refutation.

structure.notes: After 7.d5 the centre is fixed asymmetrically with Black pressing along the half-open e-file and queenside, which I read as semi-open Benoni type; low confidence versus closed.

approach.notes: An established sideline of the Sämisch, standard at a high level.

level.notes: Black must understand King's Indian Benoni-type plans and the sharp sidelines; advanced by understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6...Nc6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. f3 O-O 6. Bg5 Nc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black plays for ...e5 and a closed King's Indian structure instead of the Benoni-type c5 plan.

character.reason: Opposite-side attacking plans with the centre fixed.

structure.reason: After 7.d5 Black presses on the half-open e and b files in a Benoni-type centre.

approach.reason: A sideline of the Sämisch, not a system.

level.reason: King's Indian Benoni-type plans and theory.

plans.reason: White gains space with d5; Black expands on the queenside.
